title: A scalar under the non-specific tag becomes an integer without the tag
notes: The non-specific tag `!` makes a scalar a string (Example 6.28). Left in place it would make the new `7` the string "7"; setters are exact, so the tag goes. Dropping a tag that contradicts the new value is a kit convention.

provenance.reference: A writer that kept the non-specific tag, so the edited value read back as the string "7" instead of the integer 7.
